organizations.normalization_notes: The university is modeled as William Bascom's employer because Northwestern identifies him as a faculty member; his prior student status is not substituted for employment.
The source calls the agency the Works Progress Administration. That historical form is preserved even though the agency was renamed the Work Projects Administration in 1939.
Modeled as a military assignment, not a civilian employer. The source does not name the Wisconsin college where Basehart instructed.

affiliations.date_precision: Northwestern states that Bascom continued as a faculty member after his 1939 doctorate. A peer-reviewed history places his COI interviews and volunteer recruitment in January 1942; an exact separation date is not stated.
affiliations.research_notes: The scholarly article cites Bascom's Box 41 personnel file and January 1942 COI correspondence. Northwestern independently documents his faculty role. No intervening employer is documented.

affiliations.date_precision: The appreciation dates the position to 1941 and states that Basehart was drafted early in 1942. Exact appointment and separation dates are not supplied.
affiliations.research_notes: This is the last documented civilian position before Basehart's Army service. It is not labeled immediate pre-OSS because Army training and assignments intervened.

affiliations.role_title: Instructor at an unnamed Wisconsin college
affiliations.date_precision: The appreciation places the assignment after Basehart's 1942 commissioning and says that he was sent to Africa as chief of an OSS mission the following year. Exact months and the college are not supplied.
affiliations.research_notes: Published as the best-supported immediate military predecessor. The source does not exclude a brief intervening assignment, so the dates remain year-level.

claims.claim_text: The indexed William R. Bascom is high-confidence matched to the Northwestern anthropologist recruited into the Coordinator of Information in January 1942.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The peer-reviewed study cites the Box 41 personnel file by exact name and reconstructs Bascom's January 1942 COI recruitment from archival correspondence.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the exact full name, exact Box 41 personnel-file citation, distinctive profession, Northwestern connection, and matching early intelligence chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: The article dates the COI interviews and volunteering to January 1942 and the field deployment to April 1942.
claims.match_notes: High rather than confirmed because this project has not directly examined the physical Box 41 file cited by the authors.

claims.claim_text: William R. Bascom was a Northwestern University anthropology faculty member immediately before his January 1942 COI recruitment.
claims.evidence_excerpt: continued as a faculty member of the department
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Northwestern documents Bascom's faculty role after his 1939 doctorate; the scholarly chronology places his COI interviews and volunteering in January 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact-name Box 41 citation and the distinctive Northwestern anthropologist biography support the same person.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded: faculty service followed the 1939 doctorate, and COI recruitment occurred in January 1942; no intervening affiliation is documented.
claims.match_notes: The claim does not infer an exact separation day. It is included in employer analytics because the role is explicitly faculty employment.

claims.claim_text: Northwestern University is the last documented civilian employer before William R. Bascom entered wartime intelligence work.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The institutional faculty history and the January 1942 COI recruitment chronology form a continuous, strongly date-bounded sequence.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The uncommon full name, profession, university, and direct Box 41 citation support one person.
claims.temporal_assessment: No source reviewed identifies an intervening employer between Northwestern faculty service and the January 1942 COI interviews.
claims.match_notes: Published separately from the immediate-affiliation claim so the two research questions remain auditable even though they currently name the same institution.

claims.temporal_assessment: The appreciation dates Army entry to early 1942, the OSS mission to the following year, and release as a captain in 1946.
